criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report has a recognisable structure, an executive summary, labelled visual material, and a bibliography. Presentation is weakened by grammatical errors, inconsistent figure/table labelling and formatting, incomplete reference details, and use of Wikipedia despite the task explicitly disallowing it. Several claims and design decisions are not adequately cited.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction of a Earth observation satellite

technical_issues.issue: The report says RAAN's initial value indicates the launch facility location. RAAN defines the inertial orientation of the ascending node; it is not determined by the launch site's location alone.

The report calls the orbit retrograde but later describes its paths as near-polar without giving a selected local solar time or node-time requirement. A sun-synchronous orbit provides a consistent local solar time, but does not by itself guarantee the claimed imaging illumination conditions.

The claim that a near-polar orbit gives significant contact for the vast majority of passes is not established. Access depends on station latitude, geometry, elevation mask, and orbit; the listed access windows instead show intermittent contacts.

The text claims an average contact duration of almost ten minutes, while the stated mean is 580.786 seconds, approximately 9.68 minutes. The table also has inconsistent access numbering and reports only a subset of the access periods.

The 600 km altitude and 250 km reef width are not connected to a sensor field of view, ground sampling distance, or imaging performance calculation, so the proposed coverage and resolution trade is unsupported.

The five-year lifetime is asserted without spacecraft reliability, power, propellant, or orbital-decay analysis. A drag sail is a plausible passive disposal concept, but its deployment and compliance with applicable disposal limits are not demonstrated.
Vega E is presented as a planned option for a 2025 launch despite being a future launcher in the report's timeframe; the proposed rideshare, orbit compatibility, and launch date are not confirmed.
Reference [6] cites Wikipedia, which the assignment explicitly disallows; several other entries are incomplete and do not provide consistent author, title, date, or access information.

overall: A coherent preliminary concept with useful STK access output and a reasonable single-satellite rationale, but key operational and orbital claims need correction or substantiation. The absent software files, uncertain launch plan, incomplete user definition, and weak sourcing limit confidence in the design.

feedback.summary: You present a coherent coral-monitoring concept, explain the value of a single spacecraft, and include STK access results. To reach the next rubric level, strengthen the evidence behind key design choices, resolve inconsistencies in orbit and communications claims, and provide a more complete, professionally presented report with reliable references.
next_steps: In Orbit and Ground Control & Communications, correct the RAAN explanation and clarify the selected orbit’s local solar time. Use the actual station geometry and access windows to support contact frequency and duration, and connect altitude and reef width to sensor field of view, ground sampling distance, and imaging performance.

In Launch and Mission Duration & EOL, verify that the launch vehicle, date, rideshare, and target orbit are feasible. Support the five-year lifetime and drag-sail disposal plan with relevant reliability, power, propellant, orbital-decay, and disposal-compliance evidence; include the software project files or reproducible design evidence.

In the Introduction, Conclusion, and Bibliography, identify the operator and clarify the operating arrangement, evaluate whether the evidence supports mission performance, and replace Wikipedia with complete, consistent, credible references. Proofread grammar and standardise figure and table labels and formatting.
